findings.description: The screen is held up to be read and is in sharp focus from 00:06.75 to 00:09.00, but its text is pseudo-text. The header is two A's joined by a stray bar ('A‾A'). The main code has a detached hook over the 'A', an odd mid-dot, and a stray superscript squiggle. The subline has a malformed '1' and a meaningless 'x2' glyph. None of these is a coherent app UI label, word or code format.

The header reads 'A_A' consistently from 00:03.75 to 00:08.75. At 00:09.00 it reads roughly 'A7'/'A/' with the second A gone. The UI shows no navigation or change. Some motion smear is present in this frame, which lowers confidence.

In the early soft-focus frames (sharpest at 00:03.00) the code reads 'A742' with plain glyphs and no dot between 7 and 4. From 00:06.75 it reads 'A7·42' with a prominent mid-dot and a detached hook over the 'A'. The difference may partly come from defocus hiding fine detail, so this is only a possible glyph drift.

The clock at the top centre reads '4:41' at 00:03.75 to 00:04.00 and '4:49' (with a malformed final 9) from 00:04.25 onward. That is an 8-minute jump within half a second of continuous footage. The digits are small and partly blurred.
